figures.alt: How acid rain is produced, downloadable IGCSE & GCSE Biology revision notes

specPoints.text: know that, in car engines, the temperature reached is high enough to allow nitrogen and oxygen from air to react, forming oxides of nitrogen
explain how the combustion of some impurities in hydrocarbon fuels results in the formation of sulfur dioxide
understand how sulfur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen contribute to acid rain

primer.text: From Combustion you already know that fuels burn with products decided by their ingredients. This note adds the two pollutant families: nitrogen oxides born in hot engines, and sulfur dioxide from impurities in the fuel, then follows both into the rain that turns acidic.

lessons.title: Hot engines and dirty fuels
lessons.opening: Two very different sources feed the same pollution story. In the engine, sheer heat welds air nitrogen to oxygen; in the fuel, sulfur impurities burn along with the hydrocarbons.
keyPoints: Nitrogen and oxygen from air react in the high temperature and pressure inside internal combustion engines.
The products are the oxides of nitrogen, NO and NO2, also formed in blast furnaces.
Exhaust gases also carry unburned hydrocarbons and carbon monoxide, so cars fit catalytic converters to render them harmless.
Fossil fuels are contaminated with small amounts of sulfur impurities, which burn to sulfur dioxide.
The burning of the impurity follows S + O2 -> SO2, and nitrogen oxides also add to smog and asthma difficulties.

low.restatement: Engines run so hot that the nitrogen in air joins with oxygen, making NO and NO2. Fuels also carry a little sulfur, which burns to the choking gas sulfur dioxide. One pollutant is born of heat, the other rides in with the fuel.
low.analogy: One pollutant is forged by heat alone, like sparks off a grinder; the other was hiding in the fuel all along, like grit in the coal scuttle.
low.examPointer: Keep the two origins separate in answers: air nitrogen plus engine heat for NOx, fuel impurity for SO2.

medium.restatement: Inside internal combustion engines the temperature is high enough for nitrogen and oxygen from air to combine, giving the oxides NO and NO2, a route also found in blast furnaces. Separately, fossil fuels carry sulfur impurities that burn with the fuel, so the sulfur is oxidised to sulfur dioxide in the reaction S plus O2 giving SO2.
medium.analogy: The engine is a forge that welds the two air gases into new pollutants, while the fuel smuggles its own extra element into the fire like a stowaway revealed only at burning.
medium.examPointer: Quote the equation S + O2 -> SO2 for the impurity route and state the high-temperature condition for the engine route.

check.stem: Where do the nitrogen and oxygen that form NOx in car engines come from?

options.text: From the air drawn into the engine
options.explanation: Air is roughly four-fifths nitrogen and one-fifth oxygen, and engine heat welds them together.

options.text: From the petrol molecules themselves
options.explanation: Hydrocarbons carry no nitrogen; the gases come from the air the engine breathes.

options.text: From the catalytic converter
options.explanation: The converter cleans exhaust gases; it is not the source of the nitrogen oxides.

options.text: From the sulfur impurities in the fuel
options.explanation: Sulfur impurities produce SO2, a separate pollutant family.

check.stem: What condition inside an engine allows nitrogen and oxygen to react?

options.text: The very high temperature and pressure reached there
options.explanation: Ordinary air is unreactive; only engine-level heat and pressure push the two gases together.

options.text: The cold of the exhaust pipe
options.explanation: Cold ends the chemistry; the reaction happens in the hot combustion chamber.

options.text: The presence of water in the fuel line
options.explanation: Water plays no part in forming nitrogen oxides.

options.text: A spark plug made of platinum
options.explanation: The spark ignites fuel; it is the temperature and pressure that form NOx.

check.stem: Balance the equation for sulfur burning: S + O2 -> ?

options.text: SO2
options.explanation: One sulfur atom joins two oxygen atoms, the exact recipe for sulfur dioxide.

options.text: SO3
options.explanation: The trioxide needs a further step; direct burning gives the dioxide.

options.text: H2SO4
options.explanation: Sulfuric acid forms later in rainwater; the flame product is the dioxide gas.

options.text: S2O
options.explanation: That formula matches neither the atom counts nor the named product.

check.stem: Why does sulfur dioxide appear in the exhaust of a petrol car at all?

options.text: Because the fuel carries sulfur impurities that burn with it
options.explanation: The combustion of the impurity is the route; no petrol molecule contains sulfur by design.

options.text: Because nitrogen in air reacts with sulfur
options.explanation: Air nitrogen heads down the NOx route; the sulfur burns with oxygen instead.

options.text: Because the converter manufactures it from clean gases
options.explanation: Converters destroy pollutants; they do not create sulfur dioxide.

options.text: Because sulfur dissolves from engine oil into the exhaust
options.explanation: The route is the burning fuel impurity, not oil leaching.

check.stem: Besides acid rain, which adverse effects do nitrogen oxides have?

options.text: Photochemical smog and breathing difficulties for people with asthma
options.explanation: The note lists smog and asthma-linked breathing trouble alongside acid rain.

options.text: They dye surfaces black with soot
options.explanation: Soot belongs to incomplete burning of fuel, not to nitrogen oxides.

options.text: They cool the engine cylinders
options.explanation: Engine cooling is unrelated to exhaust chemistry.

options.text: They have no effects beyond acid rain
options.explanation: Smog and breathing effects are explicit in the note.

lessons.title: The road to acid rain
lessons.opening: Both pollutant families end in the same place: dissolved in raindrops, falling as acid. This lesson writes the two routes to acid rain and lists the damage the droplets do on landing.
keyPoints: Sulfur dioxide from burned fuels dissolves into raindrops and makes sulfuric acid.
The route is 2SO2 + O2 + 2H2O -> 2H2SO4, one component of acid rain.
Nitrogen dioxide from car engines reacts with rain water to give a mixture of nitrous and nitric acids.
The nitrogen route is 2NO2 + H2O -> HNO2 + HNO3, and lightning can also trigger NOx formation.
Acid rain corrodes metals and carbonate statues, harms aquatic life, pollutes crops and water, and irritates lungs.

low.restatement: Sulfur dioxide and nitrogen dioxide both dissolve in raindrops and turn the water acidic. The falling rain then attacks buildings, metalwork, lakes and lungs. Both routes end the same way, with acid carried down by falling rain.
low.analogy: The sky becomes a slow rinse cycle: pollutant gases wash into every droplet, and the whole cloud wrings out a weak acid bath over everything below.
low.examPointer: Name both acid products, sulfuric from SO2 and nitric plus nitrous from NO2, when explaining how acid rain forms.

medium.restatement: Sulfur dioxide dissolves in rainwater and, with more oxygen, forms sulfuric acid by 2SO2 + O2 + 2H2O giving 2H2SO4. Nitrogen dioxide reacts with rain water to give nitrous and nitric acids in the ratio 2NO2 + H2O giving HNO2 + HNO3, and the acid droplets fall when clouds grow heavy, corroding structures and ecosystems.
medium.analogy: Two rivers feed one polluted lake: the sulfur river runs from impure fuel, the nitrogen river from hot engines, and where they merge in the clouds the rain arrives already acidic.
medium.examPointer: Balance each route equation, then attach at least two damages, such as corrosion of carbonate rock and harm to aquatic organisms.

check.stem: Which acid forms when sulfur dioxide dissolves in rainwater with oxygen?

options.text: Sulfuric acid
options.explanation: The balanced route 2SO2 + O2 + 2H2O -> 2H2SO4 names the acid directly.

options.text: Nitric acid
options.explanation: Nitric acid belongs to the nitrogen dioxide route, not the sulfur one.

options.text: Hydrochloric acid
options.explanation: No chlorine is present anywhere in this story.

options.text: Carbonic acid
options.explanation: Carbonic acid comes from carbon dioxide in water, a different gas.

check.stem: What mixture forms when nitrogen dioxide reacts with rain water?

options.text: A mixture of nitrous and nitric acids
options.explanation: The equation 2NO2 + H2O -> HNO2 + HNO3 delivers one of each acid.

options.text: Sulfuric acid only
options.explanation: Sulfuric acid is the sulfur dioxide route; NO2 makes the two nitrogen acids.

options.text: Nitrogen gas and hydrogen gas
options.explanation: The reaction makes acids, not free gases.

options.text: Only nitric acid, with nothing else
options.explanation: The note is explicit that a mixture of nitrous and nitric acids forms.

check.stem: Which event, besides engines, can trigger nitrogen oxide formation in air?

options.text: Lightning strikes
options.explanation: The note records lightning as a natural trigger for nitrogen monoxide and dioxide formation.

options.text: Rainfall on limestone
options.explanation: That is a weathering story, not a nitrogen oxide source.

options.text: Volcanic sulfur release
options.explanation: Volcanoes feed the sulfur family; lightning feeds the nitrogen one.

options.text: Plant photosynthesis
options.explanation: Photosynthesis consumes carbon dioxide and releases oxygen; it makes no NOx.

check.stem: Which damage is caused by acid rain according to the note?

options.text: Corrosion of metal structures and carbonate statues
options.explanation: The note lists corrosion of metals, buildings and carbonate rock among the impacts.

options.text: It strengthens concrete buildings
options.explanation: Acid attack weakens and corrodes; nothing is strengthened.

options.text: It bleaches the colour from fabrics only
options.explanation: Fabric bleaching is not in the damage list; crops, water and lungs are.

options.text: It has no effect on living things
options.explanation: Damage to aquatic organisms and irritation of lungs and eyes are explicit.

check.stem: How do the acid droplets eventually reach the ground?

options.text: Cloud droplets grow heavier as they rise and cool, then fall as rain
options.explanation: The note tracks droplets growing with cooling until they are heavy enough to fall as acid rain.

options.text: The acids fall as dry powder from the clouds
options.explanation: The acids travel dissolved in water droplets, not as powder.

options.text: They sink to the ground as heavy gas
options.explanation: The delivery is rainfall, not a gas pouring downhill.

options.text: They never reach the ground at all
options.explanation: Falling as acid rain is the entire point of the formation story.

glossary.definition: The gases NO and NO2 formed when nitrogen and oxygen from air react at engine-level heat and pressure.
The gas SO2 formed when sulfur impurities in fossil fuels burn in oxygen.
A part of a car exhaust system that renders harmful exhaust gases harmless.
Rain made acidic by dissolved sulfur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen forming sulfuric, nitrous and nitric acids.
Haze formed in air through the action of light on pollutant gases such as nitrogen oxides.
